The only issues labeled **pre-v1** are #2690 and #2711. #2711 is blocked on an upstream release we don't control. #2690 — the actual v1 act — is the **irreversible owner-gated publish**: bump to 1.0.0, `cargo publish` nmp-* to crates.io, publish @nmp/* to npm, prove external consumption. Its issue-blocker (#1626) is closed and master CI is green, so the framework is *ready*, but I will **not** autonomously publish 1.0.0 permanently to public registries — that needs your go. [...] **BOTTOM LINE:** There is NO genuine framework code work in these four blocking v1. #2927 is already done (close it). #2864, #2858, #2974 are all post-v1 (feature app / dev tool / non-v1-claimed MLS feature) and should be labeled phase:post-v1 so they stop looking like un-phased p2 blockers against #2690's "zero open p2 besides #1626" bar. Consistent with the owner's steer: an issue existing ≠ it must ship in v1. v1 remains what #2690 says it is — the owner-gated publish act (name → rc rehearsal → 1.0.0 tag → crates.io/npm → external-consumption proof), gated on the public-name decision and #1626, not on any of these four. [...] **The key finding, confirmed:** there is **zero genuine framework code work blocking v1**. The four ambiguous p2 epics are all post-v1. v1 is now exactly what #2690 says — the owner-gated publish act (name → rc rehearsal → 1.0.0 tag → crates.io/npm → external-consumption proof), gated only on your go, not on any pending code. [...] Assistant: I now have a clear picture. Before fanning out any agents, let me check master CI health and open PRs (memory rules: always resync + check PRs before fanout), and confirm #1626's status (the gating tail for v1). [...] Assistant: Good — master is green, #1626 (the v1 gating tail) is closed, only one open PR (#2940, release-related). Let me get the project item IDs so I can batch-set statuses. [...] So my working goal for this session is: **drive every actionable code issue to a landed PR, get opus verdicts on the subjective ones, and confirm there's zero genuine code work left blocking v1** — leaving only the publish act for you. I'll report back as agents land. [...] **#2970 (NIP-17 wss-only gate blocks nak serve) — DEFER post-v1.**
- Verdict: keep open as a test-harness task; do NOT relax the parser gate.
- Justification: Owner already confirmed (issue comment) this is a pure local-testability gap, not a defect — validated e2e vs wss://nos.lol, downgraded to p3, does not block v1. I rejected the `cfg(test)`/feature relaxation on its merits: (a) it buys nothing for Rust tests — the gate lives only in `parse_dm_relay_list`; `DmRelayCache::upsert` doesn't gate scheme, so a test can seed the cache directly; (b) it does nothing for the actual manual `nak serve` loop — that runs through an app binary, not a `cargo test` build, so `cfg(test)` never applies, and a cargo feature enabled for validation would validate the wrong confidentiality posture (a footgun + forked NIP-17 §2 invariant). Correct closures are non-invasive: an in-workspace integration test that injects a `ws://` DmRelayCache entry directly (bypassing the parser), or a cert-trusted wss local-relay recipe (mkcert in front of nak serve — the non-trivial part is client cert trust). Neither is triage-sized, so deferred to the next NIP-17 validation pass.
- Action: comment #2970#issuecomment-4881977806, label `phase:post-v1`. [...] Assistant: #2970 and #2993 → Backlog (post-v1, both correctly deferred, not forced). Remaining: #3004, #2962 (sonnet slam-dunks), #3010, #3005 (opus fixes) still working toward PRs.
